newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says Q3 crude exports up vs year ago.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says Q3 crude exports up vs year ago.

text.p: State oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Wednesday that crude oil exports rose to 1.53 million barrels per day (bpd) in the third quarter of 1996 from 1.45 million bpd in the same period last year.
Crude exports in the first nine months of 1996 rose to 1.54 million bpd from 1.34 million bpd in the first three quarters of last year.

Crude export revenues were $2.7 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.97 billion a year earlier, while in the first nine months they were $7.61 billion, up from $5.75 billion in January-September 1995. The average Q3 export price was $19.16 per barrel, up 30 percent from a year previously, Pemex chairman Adrian Lajous told a news conference.
In comparison, the average crude production price in the first nine months of the year was $2.47 per barrel, "slightly lower" than a year previously.

Lajous said Pemex was now processing just seven percent less natural gas compared to before the fatal explosion at its Cactus processing plant in the southern state of Chiapas in July, but did not give a figure. Natural gas exports resumed in September at an average eight million cfd, he said.
Lajous also said Pemex had discovered two new offshore oil fields in the third quarter, called Kanaab and Manik, as well as an extension to the Escuintle field, and was evaluating their reserves.
